title: Array Traversal: Find the Maximum
oneLiner: Same single pass, different accumulator: track the best-seen value instead of a sum.
keyTakeaway: The "one pass, one accumulator" shape isn't just for sums -- swap the accumulator's update rule (compare-and-replace instead of add) and the same loop finds a max, min, or first match.
explanation: Same shape as the last lesson -- one pass, one pointer -- but instead of accumulating a sum you're accumulating a "best value seen so far." This compare-and-maybe-replace move shows up constantly: finding a max/min, finding the first element that satisfies some condition, tracking a running best for a greedy algorithm. Watch out for the seed value: starting your "best so far" at 0 silently breaks on an all-negative array.

visualizationSteps.message: Seed "best so far" with the first element (3) -- never seed it with 0, an all-negative array would break that.
Index 1 (value 9) beats the current best -- new best is 9.
Index 2 (value 2) doesn't beat 9 -- best stays the same.
Index 3 (value 17) beats the current best -- new best is 17.
Index 4 (value 6) doesn't beat 17 -- best stays the same.
Index 5 (value 11) doesn't beat 17 -- best stays the same.
